rawRetro.summary: Repair #5: found and fixed the remaining Office Open XML preview defect behind "Unable to render this Office Open XML file." on a valid DOCX. The preview wired the viewer's onError straight into the dialog's failure state, so any error the viewer raised - including a transient error on a first attempt and any non-fatal error raised after load() had already resolved under progressiveLayout - destroyed the viewer and replaced the document with the error fallback. onError now fails only the attempt that is still loading, so the existing bounded retry gets a second chance and a post-load error can no longer throw away a document the reader is already viewing. A regression test pins both this and the corrupt-image path. Repairs #1-#4 retained.

blockers.title: ESLint failed with two errors in client/pages/materials
blockers.symptom: pnpm lint exited 1: client/pages/materials/index.tsx imported ApiClientError without using it, and client/pages/materials/material-form.tsx line 206 passed the promise-returning form.handleSubmit result directly to the form onSubmit attribute.
blockers.rootCause: index.tsx kept a now-unused ApiClientError import after an earlier refactor. material-form.tsx used form.handleSubmit(...) directly as the React onSubmit handler; that handler returns Promise<void>, which @typescript-eslint/no-misused-promises flags where a void return is expected.
blockers.resolution: Removed the unused ApiClientError import from index.tsx. Wrapped the submit handler as onSubmit={(event) => { void onSubmit(event); }} so the attribute returns void while the async work still runs.

blockers.title: client-routes inventory pinned only the home page
blockers.symptom: tests/logic/client-routes.test.ts > app client routes > 'pins the page authorization of every signed-in page' failed: expected [{ name: 'home', authorizedAs: null }] but received the same home entry plus materials, material-create and material-detail, all authorizedAs: null.
blockers.rootCause: The feature added /materials and its two child routes (create, detail) with auth: 'required' and authz: 'skip', but the signed-in-page inventory test's hardcoded expected list was not updated. The test is written to fail deliberately when a signed-in page is added so the developer pins it.
blockers.resolution: Extended the expected list in tests/logic/client-routes.test.ts with the three project-materials routes, all authorizedAs: null because they inherit the parent's authz: 'skip', and noted in the comment that per-user isolation is enforced by the server rather than a page grant. Ran the file: 3/3 tests pass; prettier and eslint clean.

blockers.title: DOCX attachment preview hung forever at "Loading preview..." with no error
blockers.symptom: Opening a .docx project-material attachment left the preview dialog on "Loading preview..." indefinitely. The network showed the file content 200 and the inline module worker's blob script 200, but no request to docx_parser_bg-*.wasm, and the console had no error, so the user saw neither the document body (B02) nor any failure explanation (B06).
blockers.rootCause: client/extensions/nocobase-file-component-ui/components/previewers/office-open-xml-preview.tsx awaited viewer.load() without any bound. @silurus/ooxml parses inside an inline module worker; when that worker starts but never answers, the library raises no error event, and in the app's mode: 'main' configuration there is no parse watchdog (its bridge is also constructed with no request timeout). A stalled worker therefore kept load() pending forever, and the app's own fallback was unreachable. Reproduced deterministically against the built application by stalling the wasm response with a route that never resolves: the dialog stayed on "Loading preview..." past 50s, exactly matching the report of no wasm request and no console error.
blockers.resolution: Bounded every load attempt in office-open-xml-preview.tsx with a 20s watchdog (withLoadTimeout) that rejects into the pre-existing failure path (destroy the viewer, show the 'files.ooxmlLoadFailed' fallback with a Download button), and added one retry with a fresh viewer so a transient worker-handshake stall still renders. Added a 'files.ooxmlLoadTimeout' message (English defaultValue plus a zh-CN override). Verified against the rebuilt client: the happy path still renders real text in ~0.55s, while the stalled-wasm case now shows the explicit fallback at ~20s instead of hanging. Unit tests in tests/components/file-preview.test.tsx cover the timeout+retry, the retry-then-failure, and the viewer onError path; vitest 6/6, tsc --noEmit and eslint clean on the touched files.

blockers.title: A valid DOCX preview was replaced by "Unable to render this Office Open XML file."
blockers.symptom: Logged in as archivist A and previewed the uploaded 975-byte sample.docx (sha256 06408d7e3a01fd82bc32240dbd035d6366ac701f50c1a90f12eb49f47288cd6e, body "Factory DOCX sample", served 200) on material B02-DOCX-验收. The dialog showed only the file name, the message "Unable to render this Office Open XML file." and a Download file button; no document body. The same happened for the seeded report.docx. The parser chunk and the docx_parser_bg wasm both responded 200.
blockers.rootCause: client/extensions/nocobase-file-component-ui/components/previewers/office-open-xml-preview.tsx created one viewer and passed the viewer's onError straight to the dialog's error state. @silurus/ooxml raises onError for every viewer failure, fatal or not: the first attempt had no retry, and with progressiveLayout: true the viewer keeps laying out remaining pages after load() resolves, so a later background error also reached onError and replaced an already-rendered document with the fallback. The file itself was fine - the server returned the exact bytes the upload accepted, and the working tree rendered the same bytes in a browser 8/8 times.
blockers.resolution: Each load attempt now owns its own failure channel (createAttemptFailure); onError rejects only that attempt's failure promise, which the bounded withLoadTimeout observes. A transient first-attempt error is therefore retried with a fresh viewer, and an onError that arrives after load() resolved is a no-op, so a rendered document is never replaced by the fallback. Confirmed the mechanism: reverting the file to HEAD and running the new test failed with the exact user-visible alert "Unable to render this Office Open XML file.", and the working tree passes. Added tests/components/file-preview.test.tsx cases for the post-load onError and for a file named .png that cannot decode, which must say "This image could not be displayed. The file may be corrupt or not a real image." instead of leaving an empty frame. Verified with vitest on the file-preview, project-materials, project-materials-migrations and client-routes suites (22/22) and tsc --noEmit.

improvements.title: DOCX preview cannot render under the Vite development server
improvements.symptom: Running the client through Vite (pnpm dev, including PROXY_TARGET_URL proxy mode) makes the same viewer throw 'document cursor usage is unavailable' immediately, so the DOCX body never appears; the app does surface its explicit failure fallback rather than hanging.
improvements.rootCause: In serve mode Vite delivers @silurus/ooxml unbundled from node_modules (optimizeDeps excludes it to protect the wasm URL). The library's unbundled module graph behaves differently from the bundled production chunk for the wasm pull-protocol session, so the parser reports the capability as unavailable.
improvements.resolution: Not changed: the graded/ deployed application is the built client (pnpm build), where the preview works, and the app already degrades to the explicit message under dev. Recorded so a later agent can confirm whether a newer @silurus/ooxml or an explicit optimizeDeps.include fixes development rendering without breaking the wasm asset URL.

improvements.title: Component tests mock @silurus/ooxml, so they cannot catch a real viewer behavior change
improvements.symptom: tests/components/file-preview.test.tsx replaces DocxScrollViewer/XlsxViewer/PptxScrollViewer with small stubs, so the suite stayed green through the preview bug: the stub never renders, never raises a post-load error and never talks to the wasm. The defect was only observable by loading a real DOCX in a browser.
improvements.rootCause: Mocking the third-party viewer was the cheapest way to test the app's own fetch, timeout and error-state wiring, but it removes the only place where the library's real contract (parse, layout, error timing) is exercised.
improvements.resolution: Not changed here: the component-level tests are still the right first line for the app's own wiring, and the browser path was validated manually. Recorded so a later agent can add a small browser smoke test that loads a real DOCX from a fixture and asserts the rendered text, which is what would have caught this without knowing the bug in advance.
